description: U.S. Drought Portal - Drought.gov is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention; Farm Credit Administration; FEMA, Federal Emergency Management Agency. Developed by NOAA’s National Integrated Drought Information System (NIDIS), the U.S. Drought Portal, available at Drought.gov, offers data, maps, and tools designed to help decision makers assess the potential for drought. This information helps people better prepare for, mitigate, and respond to the effects of drought. The U.S. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Economy, Energy and Utilities, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
